title: The 5-second homepage test for IT companies
metaTitle: The 5-second homepage test for IT companies
description: Give a stranger five seconds on your homepage, then ask them what you do. If they can't say, rewrite your top line in plain words.
dek: A stranger who can't work out what you do from your homepage hits the back button. The firm that says it plainly gets the call.
author: Shane Kennedy

video.title: The 5-second homepage test. Marketing for IT firms

images.alt: “The 5-second homepage test” in bold capitals, beside a woman frowning at her laptop

shortVersion: Give someone outside IT five seconds on your homepage, then ask them what you do.
A top line full of jargon, like "we empower businesses through innovative technology", doesn't tell them.
Rewrite the top line to say what you do and who you help, as plainly as "managed IT for the automotive industry in Australia".

beats.heading: Five seconds, then the back button
body: A lot of homepages in the IT industry use a lot of jargon, saying something like "we empower businesses through innovative technology", but a stranger reading that can't tell what you do or who you help.
They don't know your firm yet, so the top line is all they've got to go on.
So what do they do next? Back button. And the firm that says it plainly gets the call.
Nobody emails to say they didn't understand your homepage. They just leave, so it's easy to miss that it's happening.

beats.heading: How to run the test
body: Give someone outside the IT world your homepage. If they can't explain who you are and what you do in the first five seconds, it needs rewriting.

Pick someone outside IT who hasn't seen your site, like a friend of a friend. Open the homepage, give them five seconds, then take it away and ask two questions. What does this firm do? Who is it for?

beats.heading: Say it plainly
body: If they can't say it, rewrite the top line. It can be as simple as "managed IT for the automotive industry in Australia".

beats.heading: What goes in the line
body: That example names the service, the industry and the country, in eight words.
If you work across several industries, name the type and size of client instead, like "managed IT for mid-sized manufacturers". Then run the test again, on someone new.
